[Music] My name is Nikhil John, I am from St. Teresa’s Parish in Pakki.
The reason I came here to Kottayam was because of my job. My job was the most important thing for me.
I came here and took the Marian covenant. It was on March 17, 2025,
that I signed the Marian covenant. The reason for taking the Marian covenant was that—
I had been working in Bahrain for six years. From there I got a job in Saudi,
and for its paperwork, on November 7 I resigned from Bahrain and returned home.
But the paperwork went well and in a proper way.
There were some obstacles, but still it progressed. Then in January, the business visa stamp was done.
After that, there was a small delay in going. And they didn’t say anything regarding the ticket.
So the job got delayed—January passed, February passed, March came. Altogether, in those three months,
I was in a mentally down state, because financially, I was the only one supporting my family.
In that situation, it was completely difficult for me, because there were home loans and other debts.
All those things affected me a lot mentally.
I started shutting myself in my room, stayed away from social media, and even stopped answering calls from friends.
I stopped going out, and even my prayer life started to decline. During that time, on March 13,
I received their email.
The job was cancelled—they said they could not hire me. That completely put me down, and I did not tell anything to my family.
But the first thing I did was take the Bible and read. While reading, I came across a verse about “covenant.”
At that time, for me, “covenant” meant only Kreupasanam.
I had heard about Kreupasanam earlier, like everyone else, first through social media in a negative way. Later,
I began to hear good things. So on March 17, I came here to Kreupasanam with my mother,
sat here and cried and prayed. At that time, a sister sitting behind me told me:
“It is enough that you come to Kreupasanam. Mother will take care of the rest.” That’s what she said.
For the first time, I told my mother, “Amma, I lost that job. Now I need to look for another one.” Mother,
she wept a lot. The reason I came and shared this here was because I was certain that if I told it here,
Blessed Mother would surely give me a good job. That’s why I came and told it here to Amma.
After that, I took the covenant here, then went back home. For the first one or two months, in a normal way,
I prayed the covenant prayers morning and evening, gave the Kreupasanam newsletter, and that’s all I did.
I didn’t do anything much more. My only faith was that I would get a job by coming here.
That was my hope. But after one or two months,
I started to feel troubled, because I had a big doubt—whether my covenant was going correctly.
At that time, I wasn’t attending daily Mass, even though there was a church near my house.
But after a month or two, I began to attend Mass in the mornings.
I started praying. I started reading the Bible. Slowly, I was returning to some discipline.
Yet, I still felt something incomplete, because I wasn’t doing any works of charity.
Earlier, I used to donate some money to an old-age home, but apart from that, I hadn’t really done much from my side.
So I began praying more. During Mass, instead of complaints,
I started to have conversations with Jesus.
I began sharing with Him about my current matters and even my past, because complaints—Jesus already knows them.
So rather than repeating them, I started conversing with Jesus. I also started conversing with Mother.
One day, while praying in church,
I felt the need to do more works of charity. But I didn’t know where to search or how to find them.
I was also an introverted type of person, so it was very difficult for me to go and do something publicly.
But I told this to Mother, and I told Jesus, “I cannot do this. But You show me someone,
or open a way for me.” That’s what I prayed.
One day in the morning, when I went to church, I met a brother there. He told me there was a central prayer group,
that meets every Thursday at St. Antony’s, Kottayam. He just told me to come.
So I went to that prayer group. There were a few people gathered, praying together.
I joined in that prayer. There, I met another brother,
who had also taken the covenant here at Kreupasanam. He came forward and shared his testimony.
He was involved in many charitable works. One day, he told me, “Let’s also go and do such charitable works. Just come when I call.”
So he called me, and I went to a retreat center in Palai called Mariasadanam.
That’s where I began my charitable works. From that moment, many changes started happening in my life,
because until then, I had been getting interview calls,
but technically, nothing was working out. I am a software engineer. After coming back home from Bahrain,
my skills had become somewhat backward, not upgraded.
So whenever I forwarded my résumé to my friends, the first thing they told me was:
“If you submit this résumé, none of the current companies will accept it, because it has outdated technologies and things.”
I was still following the older style, which wouldn’t get me anything in the present situation.
So I was in a mentally broken state.
At that time, I told Mother, “Mother, You must now prepare my resume Yourself.”
One day, I came here and submitted my resume before Mother. I gave it to Mother.
“Amma, this resume is something that, when people look at it, it will not work.
But Amma, You must select me and give me a job.” That was my prayer.
During that time, while listening to Daily Bread in the morning, there was still no movement in the matter of my job.
Nothing was happening. At that time, while listening to Daily Bread, Fr. Joseph said,
“There are some people struggling regarding jobs.” He then mentioned some dates, some numbers,
and asked us to pray with one of those numbers.
So I chose the number seven, because Mother appeared on the seventh day. That’s why I chose seven.
But it was in the month of May that I had chosen that date. When I checked in the calendar,
the next sevens were the 17th, 27th, and then the seventh of June, and so on.
Then I was a bit afraid: “Mother, let this not be delayed too much, because financially I am struggling a lot.”
All my cash in hand was completely gone. My account was becoming zero.
I had no idea how to move forward.
Then a thought came to me: July is the seventh month. But to survive until then, financially, I was not at all stable.
It was a very difficult time. So I prayed again, but still that date seven just passed by.
Afterwards, one day while listening again to Daily Bread, during the testimony time, a sister said:
“If we are troubled in our heart, just recite the Act of Contrition.
When we pray with the Act of Contrition, God forgives our sins and we will receive some comfort.”
One morning, while sitting outside at the veranda looking at the plants, I was praying the Act of Contrition and the Act of Faith.
At that moment, I suddenly smelled jasmine flowers very strongly.
At first, I thought it was just my imagination. But for quite a while, I kept feeling it.
I looked this way and that way, to see if someone was passing by after spraying perfume.
But I saw no one. Then I ran straight to the balcony. I looked everywhere carefully,
to see if anyone was standing there. But I did not see anyone.
Still, I was continuously experiencing the strong fragrance of jasmine.
So I told Mother, “Mother, if this is You, then give me a sign—at least show me a rainbow.”
But the weather that day was not at all favorable for a rainbow.
Yet, by that evening, when I looked out into the courtyard, a rainbow appeared.
It didn’t stay for long—just enough for me to take a photo. After that, the rainbow disappeared.
Then I strongly believed: Mother is with me. Even if I don’t get a job,
Mother will still guard and care for me. That was my faith.
One day after prayer, while I was sitting, my mother asked me from home, “Do you have any money to buy groceries?”
But that day, my account was exactly zero. I had nothing in hand either.
I didn’t cry in front of them, but I went into my room, closed the door, and cried heavily.
Right then, I received a call from a company. They said, “You have an interview scheduled.”
On that very same day when I had been crying, the interview was conducted.
Usually, I attend interviews sitting in my room. But that day, in my heart, I felt:
“Don’t sit in this room. Go to the next room and attend it from there.”
I wasn’t sure if it was just my thought or not. So I prayed and opened the Bible for a verse.
The verse I got was: “Not your will, but whatever is God’s will, let that be done.”
That was the verse. Then I went straight to the next room, and there I spread the covenant salt and covenant medal everywhere,
prayed, and holding the covenant medal in my hand, I prayed.
That’s how I attended the interview. There was a reason for that. Through a testimony,
I understood that the covenant medal should be held in the hand.
Until then, I had been wearing it around my neck. Along with my scapular, I used to keep it.
It is said that if you wear it on your neck, it is an ornament, but if
you hold it in your hand, it becomes a weapon—that is the greatest strength of the covenant medal.
So, holding the covenant medal in my hand, I attended that interview. But
when I saw the job description, it was about three pages long. For me, to crack that immediately
was very difficult, because I was far behind in technology.
And I didn’t get any time to prepare for the interview. At that time, mentally I was very troubled.
During that time, instead of preparing for interviews, I was only listening to testimonies.
Then a call came—from Bahrain and Abu Dhabi.
At one of those times, my interview got scheduled. So I told Mother: “I am not attending this.
Mother must attend it. If this is from Mother, then let Mother give me this job.” That’s what I said.
So the interview call came. There were about four people on the panel.
The interview went well. Quite a lot of technical questions were asked. But for me,
I was sitting in a blank state. Yet somehow, I was saying something.
After all that, once the interview was over, by evening itself, I came to know that I was selected.
If you ask when I got selected in that interview—it was after I came here for the second time and renewed the covenant.
Only after that did I get that interview call, and I got selected. Everything happened very quickly.
On June 19th, I came here and renewed the covenant. On June 29th, I got the interview call.
I attended the interview, got the job, and everything was confirmed. Then, on July 10th, I went there and joined.
July, as I said, is the seventh month. Just as Father had said, just as I had desired,
in the seventh month itself, I got the job. Then I went to work. Later, as for charitable activities—
earlier, I had never done such things. It was only a week before renewing the covenant that I started doing charity works.
I packed food parcels and went to town, giving them to those who were hungry and to those who seemed in need.
In the same way, another charitable work I did was going to Palai, to a retreat center called Mariasadanam.
I went there and did service work for them. These were the charitable activities I was doing.
As an apostolic work, every month I used to come here, collect the covenant newsletters,
and distribute them in bus stands, churches, hospitals—wherever I could.
Each time before distributing, I would take the newsletters home,
recite the Creed over each one, fold it, mark the sign of the cross, pray, and only then would I give it to others.
Then, regarding spiritual growth—I started attending daily Holy Mass.
Without missing, I began to go for Mass every day. Then, every two weeks, I started going for confession.
I also began to say the family prayer daily, and personally, I started praying the Rosary alone in my room.
All this brought a lot of change.
Another blessing I received through the covenant was in my family prayer life.
My father is a driver. Normally, he used to be someone who would just sit nearby when we prayed,
but he would neither recite the Rosary properly nor know the prayers well.
But after we took this covenant, I placed it as an intention.
And just as I intended, my mother helped me, and my father now sits with me, reciting the Rosary and praying always.
For me, that was the greatest blessing.
In the same way, I also spoke to one of my friends and brought him here to take the covenant.
I made it my mission to do so.
“Those who fear the Lord will seek His will, and those who love Him will be filled with His law.” (Sirach 2:16)
What we can say is that Nikhil’s testimony is a very strong, adventurous apparition testimony.
This son had gone into deep despair. He was in a state where his balance had become zero.
For the sake of this son, Holy Mother created a powerful opportunity to intercede.
We know that to be an apparition witness, the qualification is unworthiness—not by merit, but by grace.
This son himself admits: “All my money was gone. All my hopes were destroyed.
What I had left was only my sorrow and my tears. I was in a condition where I could only cry, unseen by others.”
It was then that the Blessed Mother held my hand, lifted me up, and led me to Jesus—as though on a pilgrimage.
We know that what is called the covenant is a pilgrimage, a journey that continues until eternity.
What we can say about this son’s beautiful testimony is that he has received the great grace of being able to reach Jesus.
Fr. Joseph—always says, when we are in the covenant itself, Jesus gives us blessings as
incentives. Some people stop there and turn back. Only very few return with deep eagerness to attain Jesus.
Some, when they enter, renew the covenant simply to have their intentions fulfilled.
Those who reach the silver-grey stage often say this: “Now I have no more needs.” Once one or two urgent requests are
fulfilled, they say: “I need nothing else now. Jesus alone is enough for me. I need only the intercession of the Blessed Mother.”
In this son’s testimony we can see that the covenant has touched every area
of life. It is a full life testimony that he has shared with us here.
Always waiting in prayer, moving prayer away from a complaining style into a conversational one, and engaging in works of mercy and apostolic activities—
when Jesus sees his timid nature—“I can’t do this”—He gives him the great confidence of knowing there is
someone to ask, “Lord, whom should I give this to?” That is a big part of reaching Jesus.
Through the Daily Bread teaching, when Father gave the number seven, this son received it, kept asking again and again
what it meant, and approached the Word always with openness. This shows us that he has already embraced the covenant lifestyle.
When we come to a zero balance, we surrender: “Now I have no other way. I have entrusted all my
matters to You.” Like the Blessed Mother, who said, “Do whatever He tells you,” this is what the son has done.
That is the beauty of some testimonies—they show us how the covenant touches everything completely.
During his testimony confirmation, this son said: “Give me a job where I can have Holy
Mass. I cannot miss Mass. I must receive Jesus.” That deep thirst was granted to him.
This is the specialty of his job too.
If he has Holy Mass in his own country, that is good. But the job he received is in Abu Dhabi.
He can work from home—though not simply as a home job, but working from home for Abu Dhabi.
It is work from home that he will be doing. What a great grace from the Holy Spirit!
As Father says, this is the change in our lifestyle—from blessing to grace.
He also spoke about the power of the covenant medal. Like a double-edged sword, the coin vibrated strongly, and he experienced it deeply.
Living in the covenant gives us such testimonies, which are always examples for us.
For the youth, this is a great inspiration.
As Father often says, each person’s testimony can be handed over, shared.
We can join the intentions of all unemployed children, all suffering children, with this testimony.
And then give Jesus a good round of applause, offering the testimony to Him.
